llm.summary: This appears to be a legitimate VMware audit and policy helper, but it needs review because a single environment variable can disable policy enforcement across all wrapped VMware operations.

dimensions.detail: The audit, policy, sanitization, and decorator capabilities are coherent with the stated VMware infrastructure purpose, but the documented VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 switch bypasses all policy checks across a high-impact tool family.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill is not user-invocable and is disclosed as an auto-loaded dependency for VMware skills; that broad activation is expected for shared audit/policy infrastructure but should be understood before installation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation is via the declared uv package vmware-policy, with no embedded executable artifact files found; static scan and VirusTotal telemetry were clean.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill reads agent-identifying environment signals and records operational metadata for auditing; the artifacts say credentials are not stored and no network data flow is used.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persistently writes audit records, including parameters, results, agent, workflow ID, OS user, status, and risk level, to ~/.vmware/audit.db with rotation and export support; this is disclosed and purpose-aligned but sensitive.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in production. Keep ~/.vmware permissions tight, handle audit exports as sensitive data, verify the vmware-policy package/source you are installing, and do not set VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 except as a controlled break-glass action because it disables the policy guardrail while VMware operations can still run.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad activation is disclosed as part of the shared @vmware_tool decorator model and is coherent for a cross-skill audit dependency, so this is context rather than a standalone reason for rejection.
[SQP-2] expected: Local audit persistence is expected for this skill and is disclosed in multiple artifact sections, though users should treat the database as sensitive operational data.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The global VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED=1 bypass materially weakens the policy layer for high-impact VMware operations and lacks strong scoping or administrative gating in the artifacts.
[SQP-2] expected: Audit export is a normal compliance workflow, but exported logs can expose sensitive operational history and the artifacts do not emphasize handling restrictions.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The setup guide repeats the all-policy bypass without a prominent production warning, making the bypass concern material rather than merely informational.
